Minimum wages and formal employment in Vietnam

Vietnam raised its regional minimum wages sharply between 2012 and 2018 as part of a strategy to share the gains from rapid export-led growth with workers in manufacturing.

Using enterprise census data, we find that in Vietnam the minimum wage increases did not reduce employment in formal-sector firms, although some small firms shifted workers to informal contracts.

Effects on wages were large and concentrated among the lowest-paid workers, particularly in foreign-invested garment and electronics factories in the north and south of the country.
